classification_method: Compared YAML frontmatter and Markdown bodies. Classification concerns semantic authority, not hash equality. No runtime skill was modified or selected as a global replacement.

pairs.name: architect
pairs.preserve: Preserve the repo copy as the project semantic source and retain the user original for later reviewed import work.
pairs.rationale: Frontmatter matches. The repo body uses the current Pyrrhic team name and the current split war-phase pipeline; the runtime body retains the older Paradox name and an older pipeline description.

pairs.name: awwv-pre-commit-check
pairs.preserve: Keep both originals; retire the repo body's obsolete life_lessons.md checklist only in a separately owned process-skill packet.
pairs.rationale: The repo frontmatter/body still makes the retired life-lessons checklist a pre-commit gate. The runtime copy has the narrower current canon/determinism/test/ledger scope.

pairs.name: balkan-battlegrounds-historical-extractor
pairs.preserve: Preserve the runtime relationship text for a future reviewed repo reconciliation; do not replace either file automatically.
pairs.rationale: Frontmatter and extraction rules match, but the runtime body adds the maintained boundary between new BB extraction and querying the Historian knowledge base.

pairs.name: canon-compliance-reviewer
pairs.preserve: Preserve the repo canon-panel and sensitive-history rules; retain the user original as backup evidence.
pairs.rationale: The repo body carries current canon precedence, FORAWWV panel authority, faction IDs, sensitive-history and endgame routing. The runtime body omits those safeguards and duplicates an old phase-spec reference while naming retired V0.4/Phase A documents.

pairs.name: code-review
pairs.preserve: Preserve the repo's production, determinism, 188-week and provenance gates; later reconcile them through the shared change-specific validation policy.
pairs.rationale: Frontmatter matches. The runtime body lacks the repo's current combat horizon, full-suite calibration, determinism and pushed-commit integrity requirements.

pairs.name: code-simplifier
pairs.preserve: Keep separate copies.
pairs.rationale: The bodies are otherwise the same; the runtime copy says active developer instructions while the repo-shipped Claude copy says repo instructions. This is a valid host authority distinction.

pairs.name: formation-expert
pairs.preserve: Preserve both until a domain owner reconciles current pipeline/OOB facts and relocates session lessons to maintained knowledge.
pairs.rationale: The repo body has newer pipeline routing and movement lessons; the runtime body has additional OOB totals and corps-mapping policy. Each contains unique project semantics, so neither can safely replace the other.

pairs.name: frontend-design
pairs.preserve: Keep both; normalize line endings only when each owner next edits its file.
pairs.rationale: Frontmatter and normalized body text are identical; the unequal hash is line-ending/byte representation only and does not establish a stale semantic copy.

pairs.name: game-designer
pairs.preserve: Preserve the repo's current calibration and sensitive-history routing.
pairs.rationale: The runtime copy lacks the repo's live-source routing, calibration-last guardrail and atrocity consequence boundary.

pairs.name: gameplay-programmer
pairs.preserve: Preserve current repo invariants and session lessons, relocating conditional detail rather than discarding it.
pairs.rationale: The runtime body omits current determinism, ops-only, protected-control, 188-week and one-change-per-run rules plus movement authority lessons; it also duplicates a phase-spec link.

pairs.name: historian
pairs.preserve: Preserve the repo source hierarchy, OOB authority and settled-modeling facts; retain the runtime original for later audited import.
pairs.rationale: Both preserve judicial procedural posture, but the runtime copy omits current live routing, the full judicial/BB/OOB hierarchy and settled cohesion-floor history carried by the repo copy.

pairs.name: ledger-process-scribe
pairs.preserve: Adopt the runtime copy's more discriminating trigger when this skill is next owned; bodies are otherwise equivalent.
pairs.rationale: Only frontmatter differs materially. The runtime trigger covers explicit commit, validation and ledger/process requests; the repo description is narrower and process-summary shaped.

pairs.name: map-geometry-integrity-reviewer
pairs.preserve: Keep the runtime's scoped canon/determinism reads; route historical lessons through the napkin/topic index.
pairs.rationale: The repo body alone mandates broad life-lessons files. The runtime body otherwise matches and reflects the adopted conditional-reading policy.

pairs.name: orchestrator
pairs.stale_side: repo shared-policy sections before P1 reconciliation
pairs.preserve: Keep separate host entrypoints. Reconcile shared authority/cost/review semantics in the repo copy without copying Codex model or tool syntax into Claude.
pairs.rationale: The runtime copy contains Codex-specific Astra/Sol/Luna and collaboration-tool policy. The repo copy contains Claude-oriented dispatch concepts and current project routes, but its dispatcher-only ban on analysis/synthesis and mandatory twelve-role post-run loop conflict with the adopted policy.

pairs.name: propagate-to-canon
pairs.preserve: Preserve both and require an authority decision before reconciling FORAWWV wording; do not edit FORAWWV in this packet.
pairs.rationale: The runtime body adds host-specific skill paths but says never auto-edit FORAWWV, while the repo body permits edits after mandatory panel sign-off. The current user directive and delegated panel authority need explicit wording together; neither file alone is a safe replacement.

pairs.name: qa-engineer
pairs.preserve: Preserve the repo's production/calibration/determinism gates while moving the unconditional smoke triad to change-specific validation in P1.
pairs.rationale: The runtime body lacks current 188-week, full-suite calibration, determinism and one-change-per-run requirements. The repo also contains an overbroad every-change triad, so reconciliation must narrow applicability without deleting production gates.

pairs.name: quality-assurance-process
pairs.preserve: Preserve the repo's current Pyrrhic identity and active routing, then simplify duplicated startup policy through P1.
pairs.rationale: The runtime body retains the older Paradox team name and removes current command-board routing. The repo body has the current identity but still duplicates broad read requirements.

pairs.name: refactor-pass
pairs.preserve: Keep both; normalize line endings only during an owned edit.
pairs.rationale: Frontmatter and normalized body text are identical; the hash difference is non-semantic.

pairs.name: retrospective-analyst
pairs.preserve: Use the runtime frontmatter trigger on the next owned update; bodies are equivalent.
pairs.rationale: The runtime description is a concise trigger for milestone/comprehensive/periodic review. The repo description mixes trigger and workflow summary.

pairs.name: scenario-creator-runner-tester
pairs.preserve: Preserve both; reconcile current calibration safeguards with the runtime's explicit Historian boundary under domain ownership.
pairs.rationale: The repo body has current protected-control, source hierarchy, 188-week and calibration-last constraints plus session lessons. The runtime body uniquely adds explicit Historian invocation. Neither side is a complete replacement.

pairs.name: scenario-harness-engineer
pairs.preserve: Preserve repo pipeline determinism, byte-identity, 188-week and direct-tool fallback rules.
pairs.rationale: Frontmatter matches; the runtime body omits the repo's current live sources and durable harness constraints.

pairs.name: scenario-report
pairs.preserve: Keep separate tool-specific instructions; update the stale Paradox label only during a future owned runtime import.
pairs.rationale: The runtime copy correctly describes its Task/mcp_task/generalPurpose enum and discovery behavior, while the repo copy uses Claude's Task wording. The runtime's Paradox label is stale, but the principal semantic difference is host tool specialization.

pairs.name: systems-programmer
pairs.preserve: Preserve the repo engine invariants, baseline provenance and worktree safeguards.
pairs.rationale: The runtime body omits current live-source, determinism, byte-identical refactor and worktree rules.

pairs.name: technical-architect
pairs.preserve: Preserve the repo current-state, determinism and worktree-routing text while consolidating shared process in P1.
pairs.rationale: The runtime body lacks the repo's current live sources and durable architecture/worktree constraints.

pairs.name: ui-ux-developer
pairs.preserve: Preserve the repo UI review seat, player-safe information boundary, MapLibre constraint and current GUI authorities.
pairs.rationale: The runtime copy is substantially older and generic: it omits mandatory UI consultation, current GUI/WARROOM sources, player information-control rules, palette/design language and concrete accessibility review duties.

pairs.name: visual-explainer
pairs.preserve: Preserve the repo v0.4.2 metadata and current design/accessibility rules; later import only through reviewed preview/backup flow.
pairs.rationale: The repo copy is the newer upstream-shaped body with slide/prose modes, stronger Mermaid/layout checks and explicit anti-template guidance. The runtime copy allows aesthetics the repo version explicitly retired and lacks metadata.

pairs.name: writing-skills
pairs.preserve: Keep separate path wording.
pairs.rationale: The only semantic difference is which active skill root is foregrounded: repo-shipped Claude skills versus desktop Codex custom skills. Both explicitly require verifying the live path.
